idea: How to detect a leaking toilet
title: How to Detect a Silent Toilet Leak
description: Many toilet leaks are completely silent, wasting hundreds of liters of clean water every day. The most common culprit is a degraded flapper or flush valve seal at the bottom of the tank. Over time, mineral buildup or chemical degradation causes the rubber seal to warp, allowing a continuous trickle of water to pass directly into the bowl. To test for this, place a few drops of food coloring or liquid dye into the tank water and wait 15 minutes without flushing. If colored water appears in the bowl, the flapper seal is failing and requires replacement. Have you checked your toilet tank for silent leaks recently?

Deep blue dyed water fills the upper porcelain tank. At the bottom flush valve opening, a slightly warped black rubber flapper seal allows thin blue streams of water to trail down past the valve seat into the clear water of the toilet bowl below. Professional studio lighting, crisp focus on the rubber flapper valve mechanism, realistic materials and physically accurate internal components. Clean background with subtle visual negative space at top and bottom for text placement. Absolute photorealistic educational style, no text, no captions, no logos, no labels, no watermarks.
visual_story: The visual uses a clear educational cutaway of a toilet tank to demonstrate how water escapes unnoticed. The strong contrast of blue-dyed water moving past a compromised flapper seal directly illustrates the mechanical failure point, allowing viewers to immediately understand how a silent leak functions mechanically without needing complex diagrams.

on_image_text.hook: Is Your Toilet Leaking Without Making a Sound?
on_image_text.explanation: A worn flapper seal allows tank water to constantly trickle into the bowl unnoticed.
on_image_text.takeaway: Drop food coloring in the tank; if color enters the bowl without flushing, replace the flapper.
